subject: FREE BOOK OFFER: crowd-sourcing a vexing BUGS/JAGS problem (NIMBLE?) with the Dail-Madsen model

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: FREE BOOK OFFER: crowd-sourcing a vexing BUGS/JAGS problem (NIMBLE?) with the Dail-Madsen model
parts:
Dear list readers,
 
 Marc and I are writing a chapter on the famous "Dail-Madsen" model for the Volume 2 of the AHM book.  One issue that we've stumbled up against and simply cannot resolve is to get the DM model running in WinBUGS or JAGS when there are some covariate effects on some of the model parameters (this runs in unmarked using the pcountOpen function).
 
 In any case, I'm offering this problem up to the community to see if someone can solve the problem. IF you can get this running in WinBUGS or JAGS (or OpenBUGS for that matter) in a reasonable consistent way, for covariates on some of the model parameters, then you will get a free copy of Volume 2 when it comes out (or V. 1 if you wish). Plus you get a huge thanks and acknowledgement in the book!
 
In addition if someone can take the script below and provide a NIMBLE implementation, also free book for that!  We may use NIMBLE in vol 2 ....
 
 Below is a simple script which consists of a data simulator function where you provide the basic parameters including covariate effects for each parameter. Then after that is a bit of code to write out the BUGS model and call JAGS to try to fit it. In the example below we try to run it (but fail) with a covariate effect only on "lambda" (initial abundance), although covariate effects are simulated for all 4 model parameters. Recall that the Dail-Madsen model has 4 basic parameters: initial abundance (lambda), survival (phi), recruitment (gamma) and detection probability (p).
 
 JAGS always fails on the dreaded "inconsistent node" error. It seems impossible to choose decent starting values for this model....
 
 Note that the DM model simulator has 2 distinct recruitment models :  "absolute" and "per capita" as we note them in the BUGS file. Neither of those work.
 
 Note 2: the model works fine without covariate effects (I can send that script if you want to see it).
 
 Note 3: It's possible that the parameter values we use here are such nonsense that it's impossible to satisfy them. If anyone has some ideas on that which resolve the problem, then that counts as a win.
 
 Note 4: There could be errors in our code below and if you find some you only get the prize if the model runs!
 
 To claim your prize, just post a solution to this problem with any BUGS engine or NIMBLE that works if I run it.
 
Thanks all!
regards
andy
 
 


DMsimv2.fn <- function(M = 50, J = 3, T = 5, mean.lambda = 4, mean.gamma.rel = 0.5, mean.phi = 0.8, mean.p = 0.7, beta.lam = 1, beta.gamma = 1, beta.phi = -1, beta.p = -1){
# Simulation for multiple-visit data,
# constant time intervals between primary periods
# M: Number of sites
# J: Number of replicate (secondary) samples within period of closure
# T: Number of primary samples: years, seasons etc.
# mean.lambda: Initial expected abundance at cov.lam = 0
# mean.gamma.rel, mean.phi: recruitment and apparent survival rates,
#   respectively, at values of cov.gamma and cov.phi equal to 0
# mean.p: detection probability at cov. p = 0
# beta.X is the slope of parameter X (link transformed) on the respective covariate
y <- p <- array(NA, dim = c(M, T, J))
N <- matrix(NA, M, T)
S <- R <- matrix(NA, M, T-1)
cov.lam <- runif(M, -1, 1)
cov.gamma <- runif(M, -1, 1)
cov.phi <- runif(M, -1, 1)
cov.p <- array(runif(M*T*J, -1, 1), dim = dim(y))
logit<- function(x){ log(x/(1-x)) }

lambda <- exp(log(mean.lambda) + beta.lam * cov.lam)
N[,1] <- rpois(M, lambda)        # Initial state

phi <- plogis(logit(mean.phi) + beta.phi * cov.phi)
gamma <- exp(log(mean.gamma.rel) + beta.gamma * cov.gamma)

for(t in 1:(T-1)) {              # State dynamics
   S[,t] <- rbinom(M, N[,t], phi)
   R[,t] <- rpois(M, N[,(t)]*gamma)    # Simulate in 'relative' mode
   N[,t+1] <- S[,t] + R[,t]
}
for(i in 1:M){                   # Observation process
   for(t in 1:T){
      for(j in 1:J){
         p[i,t,j] <- plogis(logit(mean.p) + beta.p * cov.p[i,t,j])
         y[i,t,j] <- rbinom(1, N[i,t], p[i,t,j])
      }
   }
}

# Put observed data into two dimensions
yy <- ccov.p <- array(NA, dim = c(M, J*T))
for(t in 1:T){
   yy[,(J * t-(J-1)):(J*t)] <- y[,t,]
   ccov.p[,(J * t-(J-1)):(J*t)] <- cov.p[,t,]
}
# Output
return(list(M = M, J = J, T = T, mean.lambda = mean.lambda, mean.gamma.rel = mean.gamma.rel, mean.phi = mean.phi, mean.p = mean.p, beta.lam = beta.lam, beta.gamma = beta.gamma, beta.phi = beta.phi, beta.p = beta.p, cov.lam = cov.lam, cov.gamma = cov.gamma, cov.phi = cov.phi, cov.p = cov.p, ccov.p = ccov.p, N = N, S = S, R = R, p = p, y = y, yy = yy))
}

 
 

 


set.seed(24)
data <- DMsimv2.fn(M = 50, J = 3, T = 5, mean.lambda = 4, mean.gamma.rel = 0.5, mean.phi = 0.8, mean.p = 0.7, beta.lam = 1,
 beta.gamma = 1, beta.phi = -1, beta.p = -1)
str(data)


# Bundle data
win.data <- list(C = data$y, M = dim(data$y)[1], J = dim(data$y)[3], T = dim(data$y)[2], cov.lam = data$cov.lam)
, cov.gamma = data$cov.gamma, cov.phi = data$cov.phi, cov.p = data$ccov.p)

 

# Specify model in BUGS language
cat(file = "DM2.txt","
model {
# Priors
alpha.lam <- logit(mean.lambda)
mean.lambda ~ dunif(0, 100)    # Population growth rate
gamma ~ dunif(0, 5)            # per-capita recruitment rate
phi ~ dunif(0, 1)              # apparent survival (omega in paper/unmarked)
p ~ dunif(0, 1)                # Detection probability

beta ~ dnorm(0,0.1)

# Likelihood
for(i in 1:M){
   # State process: initial condition
   N[i,1] ~ dpois(lambda[i])
   log(lambda[i]) <- alpha.lam + beta * cov.lam[i]
   # State process: transition model
   for(t in 1:(T-1)){
     S[i,t+1] ~ dbin(phi, N[i,t])
     R[i,t+1] ~ dpois(gamma)           # 'absolute' recruitment = 'constant'
   #  tmp[i,t] <- N[i,t] * gamma      # per-capita recruitment = 'autoreg'
   #  R[i,t+1] ~ dpois(tmp[i,t])  # per-capita recruitment = 'autoreg'
     N[i,t+1] <- S[i,t+1] + R[i,t+1]
   }

# Observation process
   for(t in 1:T){
      for(j in 1:J){
         C[i,t,j] ~ dbin(p, N[i,t])
      }
   }
}

# Derived quantities: N for selected sites
}
")

# Initial values
R1 <- apply(data$y, c(1,2), max) # Use observed max. counts + 2 or even bigger as inits for recruitment
R1[,1] <- NA
N1 <- R1   # Initial population size
N1[,1:data$T] <- NA
N1[,1] <- apply(apply(data$y, c(1,2), max), 1, max)+1
inits <- function(){list(phi = 0.8, gamma=0.5, p=0.7, mean.lambda = 4, N = N1, R = R1+2, beta = 1)}

# Parameters monitored
params <- c("mean.lambda", "beta", "gamma", "phi", "p")
# params <- c("lambda", "gamma", "phi", "p", "N")

# MCMC settings
 
ni <- 10000   ;   nt <- 1   ;   nb <- 5000   ;  nc <- 3
 

library(jagsUI)
# Call JAGS from R 
system.time(out2 <- jags(win.data, inits, params, "DM2.txt", n.chains = nc, n.thin = nt, n.iter = ni, n.burnin = nb))
 
print(out2, 3)

Dear all,
 I am extremely happy to say that we have a solution to this problem thanks to Heloise Pavanato who noted that the prior for alpha.lam (on the logit scale) was not a good choice. The log(mean.lambda) fixes this problem (highlighted in red below).
 
 Lesson: be careful when copying code from other models ;)
 
regards
andy

# Specify model in BUGS language
cat(file = "DM2.txt","
model {
# Priors

mean.lambda ~ dunif(0, 100)    # Population growth rate
gamma ~ dunif(0, 5)            # per-capita recruitment rate
phi ~ dunif(0, 1)              # apparent survival (omega in paper/unmarked)
p ~ dunif(0, 1)                # Detection probability

# Likelihood
for(i in 1:M){
   # State process: initial condition
   N[i,1] ~ dpois(lambda[i])
   log(lambda[i]) <- alpha.lam + beta * cov.lam[i]
   # State process: transition model
   for(t in 1:(T-1)){
     S[i,t+1] ~ dbin(phi, N[i,t])
tmp[i,t] <- N[i,t] * gamma      # per-capita recruitment = 'autoreg'

R[i,t+1] ~ dpois(tmp[i,t])  # per-capita recruitment = 'autoreg'
     N[i,t+1] <- S[i,t+1] + R[i,t+1]
   }

# Observation process
   for(t in 1:T){
      for(j in 1:J){
         C[i,t,j] ~ dbin(p, N[i,t])
      }
   }
}

# Derived quantities: N for selected sites
}
")
